title: Inverse trigonometric ranges and an expression rewritten as a single tangent
intro: No calculator. Give exact values, use radians, and show the work for each part. Only real solutions are asked for.

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of tan−1⁡(−3)\tan^{-1}\left(-\sqrt{3}\right).

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> (an angle outside <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> such as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> earns no point)

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> returns the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> with the given tangent. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and tangent is odd, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}\left(-\sqrt{3}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of sin−1⁡(sin⁡5π4)\sin^{-1}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{4}\right).

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{5\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> with that sine is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the value is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> (not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>).

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Rewrite h(x)h(x)=sin⁡(2x)1+cos⁡(2x)= \frac{\sin(2x)}{1 + \cos(2x)} as a single trigonometric function of xx. Show the identities you use.

rubric.point: Uses <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2x) = 2\sin x\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + \cos(2x) = 2\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> (from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(2x) = 2\cos^2 x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>)
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x}</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = \tan x</annotation></semantics></math> as one function (stopping at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math> earns no point)

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2x) = 2\sin x\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \cos(2x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ (2\cos^2 x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \tan x</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C

rubric.point: Uses part B to write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and gives one correct solution

Both solutions <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, and no others

parts.sample: By part B, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. The principal value is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>; tangent has period <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> also works. At both, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + \cos(2x) = \frac{1}{2} \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is defined. The solutions are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{4\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
